forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.role_in_assembly: Provides the structural periodicity needed to reduce the problem to the fractional part of x.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is greater than 1
k is an integer satisfying 1 <= k <= n (so the sum is over n terms)
floor is applied to real numbers and returns an integer
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix an integer n greater than 1. Let f_n(x) = floor(n times x) minus the sum for integer k from 1 to n of floor(k times x) divided by k. Consider f_n as a function on all real numbers x. Determine all real x values at which f_n(x) is globally maximal, and determine the corresponding maximal value M(n) = max over real x of f_n(x).
quantifier_order: For a fixed integer n with n > 1
For real x (x ranges over all real numbers)
Choose x that achieves the maximum of the given expression over all real x

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter of the optimization problem; also upper limit of the sum

variables.name: x
variables.role: decision variable over which the expression is maximized

variables.name: k
variables.role: dummy index in the finite sum, constrained by 1 <= k <= n

variables.name: M
variables.role: the maximal value of the expression as a function of n

witness_dependencies: An optimal x (or the set of optimal x values) may depend on n
The maximal value M may depend on n

domain_restrictions: n is an integer greater than 1 (so that the finite sum from k = 1 to k = n is nonempty and denominators k are positive integers)
k ranges over integers in the closed interval from 1 to n
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n greater than 1, define f_n of a real input x as floor of n times x minus the sum over integers k from 1 to n of floor of k times x divided by k. Then for every real x and every integer z, f_n of x plus z equals f_n of x.
quantifier_order: for all integer n with n > 1

variables.name: z
variables.role: integer shift amount applied to x

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index inside the definition of f_n

witness_dependencies: none (the claim is an equality for all choices of n, x, z; no existential witnesses are introduced)

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1, every real x, and every integer z, the function f_n defined by f_n(x) = floor(n*x) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k*x)/k satisfies f_n(x+z) = f_n(x).
